------------------------------------------------------------------------


Reading from standard input fromm upstream command is basically to support special flags.
In the following example, the argument `input` expects a file or a flag representing standard input.

```r
library(argitect)
argitect(
    "input=s", "input"
)

if(input %in% c("-", "stdin")) {
    cat(readLines(file("stdin")), sep = "\n")
} else {
    cat(readLines(input), sep = "\n")
}
```

Then from command-line, standard input can be set via `-` or `stdin`:

```
~\> echo hello | Rscript pipe.R --input -
~\> echo hello | Rscript pipe.R --input stdin
```

```{r, echo = FALSE}
f = system.file("extdata", "pipe.R", package = "argitect")
cat(system(paste0("echo hello | Rscript '", f, "' --input -"), intern = TRUE), sep = "\n")
```

`input` can also be set as a positional argument, then no argument name is
needed to specify in the command-line.

```r
library(argitect)
argitect(
    "input=s#", "input"
)

if(input %in% c("-", "stdin")) {
    cat(readLines(file("stdin")), sep = "\n")
} else {
    cat(readLines(input), sep = "\n")
}
```

`main.R` is the script we used in vignette [Dispatching to sub-commands](sub_commands.html).

```
~\> cat main.R | Rscript pipe.R -
~\> cat main.R | Rscript pipe.R stdin
```

```{r, echo = FALSE}
f = system.file("extdata", "pipe2.R", package = "argitect")
cat(system(paste0("cat main.R | Rscript '", f, "' stdin"), intern = TRUE), sep = "\n")
```
